issues.legal_issue: Religious freedoms and respect for graves do not prevent relocation of graves when a feasible relocation is required to maintain public order.
material_facts: The dispute concerned competing religious ceremonies by two communities at the same site, and earlier decisions had established the rights each community could exercise there.

The court had repeatedly needed to make arrangements for ceremonies after apprehensions of violence; past events included violence and damage, and on other occasions ceremonies had to be restricted to prevent clashes.

Two graves had been added to the site in defiance of an earlier court order. A committee chairman found that moving them to another part of the site was feasible and would separate the communities’ places of worship.
The proposed relocation would allow religious observances at the graves while reducing the risk of conflict.
issues.conclusion: The graves could be relocated to maintain public order; doing so was not irreligious or destructive of fundamental rights, and the objection to relocation was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution protect religious practice and the management of religious affairs, but make those rights subject to public order, morality and health. Religious rights and the religious obligation to respect graves are therefore not absolute, and public-order exigencies can justify moving graves. Section 176(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, which permits exhumation for crime detection, illustrates that a prohibition on disturbing a corpse is not absolute. Section 144 of that Code was relevant to the history of restrictions imposed to prevent disorder. The court also relied on the earlier decisions in Suit No. 424 of 1931 and Suit No. 232 of 1934 in determining the rights claimed at the site; it cited no earlier appellate precedent for this principle.

rule.if: religious_rights_proceeding and recurring_public_disorder_risk and feasible_relocation_separates_worship_areas and graves_added_in_defiance_of_prior_order

predicates.religious_rights_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the exercise of religious rites or practices at a disputed site.
predicates.recurring_public_disorder_risk: The exercise of competing religious ceremonies has repeatedly caused or threatened violence, disorder, or restrictions imposed to prevent clashes.
predicates.feasible_relocation_separates_worship_ar: A proposed relocation is found feasible and would separate the communities’ places of worship while allowing religious observances to continue.
predicates.graves_added_in_defiance_of_prior_order: The graves proposed for relocation were placed at the site contrary to an earlier court order.

issues.definition: When a religious-rights proceeding involves recurring disorder, feasible relocation that separates worship areas, and graves added contrary to an earlier order, the graves may be relocated to maintain public order.

issues.legal_issue: A court may issue directions in pending proceedings to remove an impediment to implementing its earlier judgment.
material_facts: The court had already issued a judgment and directions concerning religious practices at the site.
The proposed relocation and related arrangements were intended to facilitate implementation of that judgment and reduce impediments to carrying it out.
The applicants sought directions in the existing proceedings to implement the committee chairman’s proposal.
issues.conclusion: The requested directions were within the court’s powers and the scope of the proceedings, and the application was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: A court’s authority to implement its judgment includes removing impediments or obstructions to implementation. Directions that facilitate carrying out the court’s earlier judgment fall within the scope of the pending proceedings.

predicates.supplementary_implementation_proceeding: A party seeks further directions in proceedings connected with an earlier judgment.
predicates.prior_court_judgment_requires_implementa: The court has issued an earlier judgment or directions that remain to be carried out.
predicates.proposed_directions_facilitate_implement: The proposed directions would remove an impediment or otherwise help carry out the earlier judgment.

issues.definition: When a party seeks further directions in connected proceedings, an earlier judgment remains to be carried out, and the proposed directions facilitate that task, the court may issue implementation directions.
